top.title: Ice hockey chiefs mull all 'avenues' for German worlds as Russia waits
top.description: FILE PHOTO - Czech Republic's Dmitrij Jaskin (L) and Russia's Sergei Plotnikov battle for the puck during the 2019 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship Bronze medal match ice hockey match between Russia and Czech Republic at the Ondrej Nepela Arena. (is associated with: «Ice hockey chiefs mull all 'avenues' for German worlds as Russia waits») Martti Kainulainen/Lehtikuva/dpa "All available avenues" are being considered by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) as it tries to find a way forward after Russia was allowed to compete in the men's world championship in Germany in May. The decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) prompted dismay among other nations, sponsors and politicians. Several countries said they would boycott games against Russia at the championship given the ongoing war in Ukraine, while sponsors said they would think about withdrawing. Germany is mulling whether to hand back the hosting rights or not give visas to the Russian team. "While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships," a statement said on Saturday. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole. The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues." The federation also confirmed that Belarus, which has helped Russia in its war on Ukraine, remains banned from international ice hockey competition. The International Olympic Committee lifted a ban on the Russian Olympic Committee in July, but it is being left up to individual sporting bodies if and how Russia is reincorporated, despite the Ukraine war still raging after four years. The IIHF opted to continue to exclude Russian teams on security grounds, but Russia appealed to the world's top sports court and won. The ruling could have implications for other sports.

top.title: Isaiah Marshall keeps progressing toward starting for Kansas football
top.description: LAWRENCE — Isaiah Marshall continues to look more and more likely of being able to start at quarterback Saturday for Kansas football, at home against UCF. Marshall, a redshirt sophomore and the team's regular starter this fall at the position, didn’t play in last week’s game at TCU as he dealt with what coach Lance Leipold would describe as a lower-leg issue. When the Big 12 Conference’s player availability reports started to come out on Wednesday this week, Marshall was listed as questionable — as were redshirt junior quarterbacks Cole Ballard and Chase Jenkins. But like Jenkins, Marshall was listed as probable on Thursday, and on Friday neither of those two were listed at all. RELATED: How to watch Kansas football vs UCF, including time, TV, streaming Ballard, of course, does remain questionable for Kansas ’ game against UCF. Ballard stepped in as the starter during last week’s loss against TCU. But having Marshall and Jenkins available would provide KU with a pair of players with starting experience, Marshall from this season with the Jayhawks and Jenkins from his time at Rice earlier in his college career. Kansas’ game against UCF is set to kick off at 2:45 p.m. (CT) in Lawerence. The Jayhawks (3-5, 1-4 in Big 12) are looking to bounce back this weekend, as they look to continue to position themselves for a bowl game this fall. top.title: Jacob Warren returning to old form in return from injury for Mason football
top.description: MASON — Jacob Warren had hopes of contributing as a running back or linebacker this fall for the Mason football team as it chased its goals. But those hopes took an early hit when Warren broke his left ankle during a four-way scrimmage in August. The break wasn't severe enough where Warren held out hope he could potentially return to the field this season. And that opportunity has come in the MHSAA playoffs. Warren has scored touchdowns the last two weeks while helping Mason capture a fifth district title in six years. That included having four carries for 59 yards and a TD in a 49-0 win over Fenton in a Division 3 district final Friday, Nov. 6. "I'm really lucky my injury was the best it could have been for the situation," Warren said. "I'm just so blessed to be able to be back on the field. "I'm so lucky to have the support system I have around me and the family, friends and coaches that supported me all the 10 weeks I was out. It's so awesome to be back on the football field." Warren has 10 carries for 110 yards and the two TDs the last two weeks. Mason coach Gary Houghton sensed Warren was getting back to his old form in recent practices and said his presence gives the Bulldogs another threat in the backfield to complement Troy Peters and Jeffrey Reisner, who each rushed for more than 100 yards Friday. "He's just a very dynamic athlete, a very smart football player and he's patient," Houghton said. "He'll let his blocks develop and he'll accelerate and go. He's just one of the quickest kids I've ever coached and just a really dynamic kid in space." Warren was cleared for a return a few weeks ago and is ready to do whatever is needed to help the Bulldogs try to extend their playoff run a few more weeks. The next step on the journey for Mason is a trip next week to Chelsea, which is where Warren suffered his injury. "I'm stoked," Warren said. "Obviously it sucked in the scrimmage the week before the first game (to get hurt). I'm just so excited to maybe get a little redemption next week. I can't wait." top.title: Tottenham dealt latest attacking injury blow after VAR madness at Leeds
top.description: Tottenham have been dealt another attacking injury blow after Mathys Tel limped off before half-time against Leeds . Tel was unable to continue after being on the end of a stamp by Jayden Bogle, who caught the Frenchman on the ankle with his studs. VAR spent over four minutes reviewing the incident to determine whether it was a red card offence, only for referee John Brooks - who didn’t even caution Bogle initially - to be told to stick with the on-field decision. This meant the right wing-back got away with the challenge scot free. “The referee’s call of no red card to Bogle for the challenge on Tel was checked and confirmed by VAR,” said the Premier League Match Centre. Should Jason Bogle have seen red for this challenge? 🟥👀 📺 Stream live on TNT Sports & HBO Max https://t.co/fRCRh6tXYB pic.twitter.com/fuK42Okkcz — Football on TNT Sports (@footballontnt) November 7, 2026 The statement added VAR Tony Harrington’s verdict to Brooks: “I'm confirming the on-field decision of no red card. There’s a lack of speed going into the challenge and he’s stepping into the tackle. Confirming a reckless challenge”. The challenge was similar to the one that saw Jean-Philippe Mateta shown red after a VAR review when Spurs played Crystal Palace last weekend. Spurs manager Roberto De Zerbi was visibly frustrated with the outcome of the review and his woes were exacerbated when Tel signalled to the bench that he would need to come off, having tried to play through the pain for five minutes. Tel was replaced by Dominic Solanke in the 43rd minute, who was dropped from the starting line-up following the Palace win. Mathys Tel was forced off during Tottenham's clash with Leeds (Getty) De Zerbi’s attacking options have already been ravaged by injury this season and the club will now be left to sweat over the extent of Tel’s setback. Savio and Mykhailo Mudryk are out until after the international break, while Xavi Simons and Wilson Odobert are continuing to work their way back from serious knee injuries, with both eyeing returns after the turn of the year. Tel has impressed for Spurs in recent weeks, scoring a stunning solo goal in their 2-0 win over Chelsea on 24 October, the club’s first victory at Stamford Bridge since 2018.

top.title: Kiwis reap rewards of gamble on 'freak of nature' Ponga
top.description: Kalyn Ponga helped Newcastle Knights reach October's NRL Grand Final [Getty Images] "He's a tough character and he was so adamant he was playing." Kalyn Ponga, in the words of his head coach Stacey Jones, was never going to miss New Zealand's Rugby League World Cup semi-final. But it was a remarkable return to action for a player whose tournament turned from dream to nightmare just over three weeks ago. In the World Cup opener against Australia in Sydney on 15 October, Ponga seemed to be enjoying a perfect New Zealand debut. Then it all went wrong. The 28-year-old scored two second-half tries but was forced off late in the game - having played for 20 minutes with a broken left forearm sustained in a tackle with Cameron Munster. The Kiwis went on to lose 24-22; Ponga required surgery. Just 23 days later, their talismanic full-back – initially named as a reserve, and then on the interchange bench – made a shock return to the starting 13 and delivered a starring performance as New Zealand overpowered Tonga 34-10 to reach their first Men's Rugby League World Cup final for 13 years. "Where sports science is these days – I saw what he had in his arm, the rod or plate was covering his whole arm," Jones said. "We didn't know until after our second-to-last training that he was going to be all right – he ticked all the boxes. Just a tough person." Ponga-inspired New Zealand reach World Cup final New Zealand sweep aside Samoa to reach Women's World Cup final Playing with black protective bandaging taped to his left forearm, Ponga was directly involved in four of New Zealand's six tries. His fancy footwork and slick handling setting up scores for Briton Nikora, Casey McLean and Xavier Willison. He largely dominated the contest with opposite number Lehi Hopoate, notably clearing out the full-back as he fumbled a grubber kick in Tonga's in-goal area for New Zealand's second try, scored by Dane Gagai. In defence, a bruising try-saving block on Demitric Vaimauga indicated no cause for concern about his wounded wing. "Obviously a freak of a player," said Kiwis captain James Fisher-Harris. "The defensive mindset he had tonight, he saved a couple of tries. That's what I love about KP. "He's a freak of nature. His leadership skills are underrated. He's really good for us, our spine especially." But while it was undoubtedly the Ponga show at the home of his NRL side Newcastle Knights, New Zealand are not just a one-man band. Gagai sparked the counter-attack for McLean's try by forcing a knock-on around halfway. Jahrome Hughes added directness with his carries and when putting boot to ball. Dead-eye kicker Jamayne Isaako mastered fierce winds to kick five out of six conversions, curling two over from the left touchline, to take his tally for the tournament to 36 from 38 attempts. top.title: Report: Bills are looking to trade for a defensive back
top.description: This is not exactly a shock, but now we have a report from a national insider about what the Buffalo Bills are looking for at the NFL trade deadline. That insider is Sports Illustrated’s Albert Breer. I recently tweeted the lack of reports this season represents a stark contrast to recent years, when the Bills were listed in essentially every trade-deadline insight article in the weeks leading up to the deadline. Now, there was one mention of the Bills’ intentions, from Breer, in late October. We wrote about here at Rumblings. It was one sentence and relatively vague compared to the rest of the mentions pertaining to other teams and trade chips. “ The Bills are looking for another piece or two on defense .” This time around, in a response to a tweet that highlighted the lack of a Bills mention in his latest trade-deadline article , Breer wrote this: I had it in my last trade column, and will add it here—The Bills are still looking in to adding a piece on the defensive side of the ball. And specifically at corner and safety. https://t.co/CkjvAiQRLa — Albert Breer (@AlbertBreer) November 7, 2026 The positions are the unexpected part. However, the Bills have recently added Tre’Davious White and Kader Kohou to the practice squad at cornerback. They just got a quality effort from Te’Cory Couch in the slot. At safety, Jordan Hancock is close to returning. Damar Hamlin is playing sound football. Geno Stone tied for the team lead in tackles with six against the Ravens on just 19 snaps, and he tipped a pass that led to Davison Igbinosun’s first career interception. According to Breer, the Bills are want to add a defensive back at the trade deadline. We’ll see if it happens.

The Philadelphia Eagles are turning to Joe Milton as their new starting quarterback in Week 9 against the New York Giants, replacing Tanner McKee. Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni had said McKee would be the starter earlier in the week, but he later changed his mind and went with Milton. Sirianni addressed the media about his QB U-turn, which he claims was a strategic move to try and unsettle the Giants. “I’m gonna tell you what I want to tell you, guys. A sixth round pick by the Eagles in 2023, McKee got three starts after Hurts got shut down for the season due to blood clots . He completed 63% of his passes for 638 yards with two touchdowns and two interceptions. Sirianni will now turn to Joe Milton, who will be making his first career start. Milton brings more of the dynamism and mobility that Hurts has, which may have played a part in why he was chosen over McKee. top.title: Patriots inducting Rob Gronkowski into team’s Hall of Fame
top.description: FOXBORO, MA - SEPTEMBER 10: Rob Gronkowski #87 of the New England Patriots celebrates after a touchdown against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Gillette Stadium on September 10, 2015 in Foxboro, Massachusetts. (Photo by Maddie Meyer/Getty Images) Maddie Meyer Legendary New England Patriots tight end Rob Gronkowski will be inducted into the team’s Hall of Fame Saturday. Gronkowski beat out fellow Patriots legends Adam Vinatieri and Logan Mankins in a fan vote to become the 38th inductee. Gronk spent 9 seasons in New England after being drafted in the second round of the 2010 NFL Draft. The Patriots won the AFC East in each of Gronk’s seasons and made the Super Bowl 5 times, hoisting three Lombardi’s. Gronkowski ranks first in Patriots history with 80 total touchdowns (79 receiving and one rushing), and his 7,861 receiving yards are second in team history. Gronk’s connection with QB Tom Brady was often unstoppable on the field during their time in New England. The two went to go on to play for the Buccaneers before Gronk retired in March of 2019. Gronk’s ceremony comes the same weekend Brady is expected to call the Patriots vs. Packers game at Gillette Sunday afternoon as a broadcaster for the first time. The ceremony is expected to begin at 1 p.m. You can watch it live on Patriots.com. Gronk will also be honored during the Patriots game tomorrow on Fox at 4:25 p.m. This is a developing story. top.title: Real Madrid 17-year-old academy talent earns comparisons to Bernardo Silva
top.description: Real Madrid 17-year-old academy talent earns comparisons to Bernardo Silva Real Madrid midfielder Marco Company is making significant progress at Valdebebas, establishing himself as one of the standout performers in the club’s Juvenil A side, earning him comparisons with Bernardo Silva within the club, reports AS . After arriving from Valencia in 2023, the 17-year-old talent has taken an important step in his development this season, combining regular involvement with an impressive contribution in front of goal. Notably, his emergence comes at an important moment for Real Madrid’s youth team, who have made an excellent start to their domestic and European campaigns. Company establishes himself as a key player at Real Madrid Company made his debut for Juvenil A last season, but it is the current campaign that has seen him become a much more influential figure. To put it in perspective, he is now the second-most-used midfielder in the squad behind Cherif Fofana. Statistically, Company is performing at an excellent level, scoring three goals and providing five assists across 485 minutes in La Liga and the UEFA Youth League. Marco Company is making waves at Real Madrid’s youth team. (Picture credit: Instagrtam/@marcocompany) His performances have helped Juvenil A maintain their strong start to the season. They have won all four of their UEFA Youth League group-stage matches and collected seven victories and one draw from eight league fixtures. Qualities that have caught attention at Valdebebas Company’s ability to influence attacking situations from midfield is one of the characteristics that has made him an exciting prospect. When he was younger, he was frequently compared to Mikel Merino because of his movement into the penalty area and ability to arrive in scoring positions. However, the assessment of his potential at Valdebebas has evolved, and those following his development now see similarities with Vitinha and Bernardo Silva, particularly in terms of his playing style and technical qualities. Real Madrid’s faith in Company’s long-term potential View this post on Instagram A post shared by Marco David Company García (@marcocompany) Real Madrid’s confidence in Company dates back to his arrival from Valencia in 2023. Back then, Atletico Madrid and Barcelona were also interested in securing his services, but the midfielder chose to continue his development at Valdebebas. The club subsequently strengthened its position by securing him with a €100 million release clause in February. Lastly, his development will be particularly important during the Under-17 World Cup, which is expected to disrupt the Juvenil A squad for around a month. Company is set to have an important role during that period, offering another opportunity to demonstrate his growing responsibility.

top.title: Josh Tongue ruled out of England tour of Australia in hammer injury blow
top.description: England have been dealt a hammer blow to their seam bowling department for the upcoming tour of Australia as Josh Tongue will miss the trip down under due to a toe injury. The news was confirmed on England Cricket ’s social media with the official X account posting: “Get well soon Tonguey. “Josh Tongue has been ruled out of England Men’s white-ball tour of Australia due to a toe injury. He will return to the UK to undergo further assessment.” There was no confirmation on whether a replacement would be called up to the squad ahead of the first of three ODIs due to be played in Australia from 13-18 November though it seems unlikely at this late stage. Josh Tongue has been taken out of England's ODI tour of Australia due to a toe injury (Getty) The ODI and T20 squads for the tour were announced three weeks ago with Tongue only included in the one day squad and the 28-year-old was due to return back to the UK following the conclusion of the ODI series alongside fellow quick bowlers Jofra Archer , Gus Atkinson, and Sonny Baker. Jamie Overton is also included in the squad so there is plenty of cover for Tongue following his withdrawal and return to England. Tongue made his One Day International (ODI) debut earlier this year in a contest against India in Birmingham. He took 1-50 from his 10 overs and has since been selected in four other one day games. His most recent outing was against Sri Lanka in the ODI Tri-Series which also included Pakistan. Tongue took 3-79 from 8.5 overs as the Sri Lankans made history by knocking off 429 runs with one ball remaining in the game. Tongue bowled the final over and had been earmarked as one of the death bowling seamers for Harry Brook ’s side. The ODI squad includeds two changes from the one that travelled to Pakistan for last month’s tri-series as Jacob Bethell returns following a knee injury and Archer is back after being rested for the tri-series. top.title: Nations Championship schedule, results, kick-off times and how to watch
top.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. France and South Africa currently top the two pools, with New Zealand also unbeaten and level on points with the Springboks. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. nigeria.title: Makinde: Tinubu’s poor planning plunged millions of Nigerians into hardship
nigeria.description: By Christopher Ameh, Bauchi Oyo State Governor and presidential candidate of the Allied Peoples Movement (APM), Seyi Makinde, has blamed the economic hardship facing millions of Nigerians on what he described as inadequate planning by the President Bola Tinubu-led administration. Makinde said major economic policy decisions introduced by the Federal Government were implemented without adequate plans and frameworks to cushion their effects on citizens, thereby worsening the economic difficulties faced by Nigerians. The APM presidential candidate spoke on Friday during a live interview on the Bauchi Radio Corporation (BRC), while in Bauchi State to flag off his 2027 presidential campaign. He argued that the immediate impact of the administration’s economic policies on Nigerians was a consequence of taking major decisions without adequate preparation and effective implementation strategies. Makinde stressed that economic reforms must be supported by proper planning and clear implementation frameworks to ensure that ordinary citizens do not bear the brunt of government policies. He said addressing the country’s economic challenges would require fundamental structural reforms and strong political will. The Oyo governor also highlighted the APM’s Reset Nigeria Agenda, which he said was designed to address the country’s challenges through a documented policy framework and the party’s manifesto. According to him, the agenda focuses on reforming critical sectors of the economy, promoting sustainable development and restoring true federalism that recognises and respects Nigeria’s diverse nationalities. nigeria.title: Obienyem faults Tinubu over claim Obi ignored erosion in Anambra
nigeria.description: Valentine Obienyem, a media aide to former Anambra State Governor Peter Obi, has faulted President Bola Tinubu over his claim that Obi did nothing to tackle erosion during his tenure as governor. Obienyem, in an opinion article sent to Vanguard on Saturday, described the allegation as unfair and contradicted by historical records, citing several erosion-control projects undertaken by the former governor and his role in securing regional and international support to address the problem. The reaction followed Tinubu’s visit to Akwa Ibom State, where he reportedly promised to develop the state’s deep seaport and accused Obi of failing to address erosion in Anambra during his administration. Obienyem linked the development to Obi’s recent remarks on the need to develop seaports across Nigeria’s coastal states, including the Calabar Port and Ibom Deep Seaport. He recalled that Obi had advocated the development of multiple ports across the country’s littoral states, citing Egypt, with about 15 ports, and South Africa, with about eight, as examples of countries that had diversified their maritime infrastructure to promote balanced economic development. On the erosion challenge in Anambra, Obienyem said the state had more than 1,000 active erosion sites, including the devastating Nanka-Agulu erosion complex, but maintained that Obi gave the problem considerable attention while in office. He cited two incidents to illustrate the former governor’s personal involvement in emergency interventions. According to him, Obi once arrived at Umuchiani, Ekwulobia, as early as 6 a.m. after receiving reports of advancing erosion threatening the Ekwulobia-Oko road and nearby buildings. He said some residents had begun dismantling parts of their houses to salvage their belongings before Obi intervened and directed that work should commence immediately. Obienyem said the erosion was subsequently arrested and stabilised, saving the road and protecting the threatened buildings from further destruction. He also recalled a similar intervention along the Nkpor-Onitsha dual carriageway, around the Omagba axis, where Obi reportedly responded to a distress call and helped prevent an endangered building from being swallowed by erosion. Beyond the emergency interventions, Obienyem said Obi, as Chairman of the South-East Governors’ Forum, advocated declaring the region an ecological disaster zone to attract urgent government attention and international assistance. He credited the former governor’s advocacy with helping to advance the Nigeria Erosion and Watershed Management Project (NEWMAP), a World Bank-assisted programme designed to tackle erosion and watershed degradation. To support the claim, he cited the remarks of former Minister of Environment, John Odey, who reportedly acknowledged Obi’s contribution during the project’s official launch in Abuja. Kalu also called for a change of mindset among Igbo people, particularly those who have traditionally focused on developing their communities while keeping away from national politics. He said their example would encourage younger generations to sustain the quest for unity and development, likening leadership to a relay race in which older generations hand over the baton to their successors. nigeria.title: Explainer: What INEC’s 2023 results in Lagos, Oyo, Osun actually reveal
nigeria.description: By Omeiza Ajayi, ABUJA Lagos, Oyo and Osun states each backed a different candidate in the February 25, 2023 presidential election, according to the results declared by the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC. Read Also: How Buhari promised me APC presidential ticket in 2022; I regret listening to him – Amaechi Peter Obi of the Labour Party, LP, won Lagos; Bola Tinubu of the All Progressives Congress, APC, won Oyo, and Atiku Abubakar of the Peoples Democratic Party, PDP, won Osun. What happened in Lagos? Lagos produced the closest of the three contests. Obi polled 582,454 votes (45.81 per cent), while Tinubu, the APC candidate, followed with 572,606 votes (45.04 per cent). The gap was 9,848 votes, less than one percentage point. Atiku trailed far behind with 75,750 votes (5.96 per cent), and Rabiu Kwankwaso of the New Nigeria Peoples Party, NNPP, had 8,442 votes (0.66 per cent). What happened in Oyo? Oyo was not close. Tinubu polled 449,884 votes (55.58 per cent), well ahead of Atiku’s 182,977 votes (22.60 per cent). His lead of 266,907 votes was the widest of the three states. Obi came third in Oyo with 99,110 votes (12.24 per cent), and Kwankwaso had 4,095 votes (0.51 per cent). What happened in Osun? Osun was nearly as tight as Lagos. Atiku won with 354,366 votes (46.88 per cent), while Tinubu had 343,945 votes (45.50 per cent), a difference of 10,421 votes. Obi finished third with 23,283 votes, and Kwankwaso had 713 votes (0.09 per cent). What the combined figures show Added together, the results tell a story that the three winners alone do not. Obi, who topped the Lagos poll, totalled 704,847 votes across the three states because he fell to third in both Oyo and Osun. Put differently, Obi’s win came by the thinnest of margins in the most populous of the three states. nigeria.title: Pope Leo begins South America tour in ‘fairly good shape’
nigeria.description: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay, where he will celebrate a Mass on Saturday, as he began a 12-day tour of South America in “fairly good shape.” Leo’s sixth international tour takes him to the continent that helped shape his priesthood, just three weeks after surgery for a tumor on his right lung. The 71-year-old pontiff will visit Uruguay, Argentina and Peru on one of the most intense papal trips in decades, meeting political leaders, prisoners and the poor, as well as old friends. Thousands of people, some waving yellow-and-white Vatican flags, lined the seafront of Uruguay’s capital Montevideo to greet him as he waved from a custom-made popemobile. But the crowds were relatively sparse in Latin America’s most secular country compared with Leo’s recent visits to France and Spain. Speaking in a half-empty Plaza Independencia, after being welcomed by left-wing President Yamandu Orsi, the pope lamented Uruguay’s high suicide rates — among the highest in the world — and appealed for healthcare to be “accessible to everyone.” He said the care he received after his lung cancer diagnosis made him think of the “many men and women who lack the means to obtain a timely diagnosis” or receive treatment. Leo will celebrate Mass on Saturday in a park in Paysandu, a city in western Uruguay, where 30,000 pilgrims are expected. He will then return to Montevideo to visit Casavalle, the neighborhood with the highest homicide rate in the capital, as well as the Catholic University and the Centenario Stadium, where he will preside over a prayer vigil for 60,000 people. Leo’s visit to Uruguay is the first to the country by a pope in nearly four decades. – In ‘fairly good shape’ – He told reporters on the plane carrying him across the Atlantic he was “in fairly good shape” following his surgery, and his advice for others facing their own cancer diagnosis was “not to be afraid.” The pontiff said he was bringing a message of “hope” to the world’s most Catholic continent. nigeria.title: Lagos ranks 28th among world’s 50 most dangerous cities – Survey
nigeria.description: By Sola Ogundipe Lagos, Nigeria’s commercial nerve centre and one of Africa’s busiest megacities, has been ranked among the world’s 50 most dangerous cities in 2026, placing 28th on a global crime index that raises fresh questions about urban safety, insecurity and the growing pressure on law enforcement. Lagos is the only Nigerian city on the ranking published by the “Numbeo Crime Index by City 2026” – a Serbia-based global data platform that compiles crowd-sourced information on crime safety, cost of living and quality of life across cities and countries. The list records Lagos with a crime index of 68.8, placing it in the high crime category under Numbeo’s classification. The index ranges from zero to 100, with scores above 60 classified as high and those above 80 as very high. Nigeria’s commercial capital is placed ahead of major cities including Damascus in Syria, New Orleans in the United States, San Juan in Puerto Rico and Santo Domingo in the Dominican Republic. According to the survey, five South African cities occupy positions among the top eight, with Pietermaritzburg taking the first position, followed by Pretoria in second place, Johannesburg in fifth, Durban in sixth and Port Elizabeth in eighth. Caracas, Venezuela, and Port Moresby, Papua New Guinea, occupy third and fourth positions respectively. Windhoek, Namibia, comes in at number 30. The figures also point to persistent safety concerns across the Americas. Brazil has five cities among the top 25, while the United States has several, including Memphis, Detroit, Baltimore, Albuquerque and St. Louis. Other cities featured in the top 50 include Kingston in Jamaica, Mexico City, Marseille in France, Manila in the Philippines, Birmingham in the United Kingdom and Houston in the United States. Numbeo’s Crime Index draws on several indicators, among them residents’ perceptions of crime, how safe they feel walking alone during the day or at night, and their experiences or concerns about robbery, mugging, car theft, burglary, physical attacks and harassment. It also considers drug-related problems, property crime, violent crime and corruption. The ranking reflects perceptions captured by Numbeo’s survey, rather than a verified ranking of reported criminal offences. It is based on surveys completed by Numbeo website visitors and not a direct count of police-recorded offences, reported criminal incidents or official national crime statistics. Numbeo processes the responses into scores ranging from zero to 100 to make comparisons between cities possible. The organisation also acknowledges that public perceptions of crime may not always correspond with official crime figures. nigeria.title: What do Airtel, Fidelity bank and Lekki Gardens have in common?
nigeria.description: By Temiloluwa Johnson A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. A telecoms giant, a bank and a property developer. On paper, nothing. On ARCON’s honours list, quite a lot. One connects millions of phone calls a day. One looks after people’s money. One builds homes. It is hard to think of three Nigerian businesses with less to do with each other. Yet on Friday, 23 October, Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens found themselves on the same list. At the ARCON Special Recognition Awards (ASRA) 2026, held at the Balmoral Convention Centre, Sheraton Hotel, Ikeja, the Advertising Regulatory Council of Nigeria honoured a small group of advertisers for compliance. Lekki Gardens was recognised in the Real Estate and Properties category, alongside honourees that included CocaCola, Peak, Moniepoint and Chicken Republic in their own sectors. So what do they have in common? Not size, and not industry. What they share is a record. None of them entered. ARCON’s Secretariat went back through every eligible advertisement it had vetted in the period under review and picked out the advertisers with the highest volumes of approved work in each sector. A technical assessment followed, then a jury, then final ratification, with an independent audit firm checking the process from start to finish. Nobody could buy, pitch or charm their way onto that list. The only way on was to keep getting it right. There is a second thing the three share, and it is the more important one. Each of them is trusted with something people cannot afford to lose. For Airtel, it is the connection. For Fidelity Bank, it is the savings. For Lekki Gardens, it is usually both, because a home is the largest financial decision most families will ever make. That is why the company treats its adverts as promises rather than slogans. “Compliance here is not a department. It is in the DNA of the business,” says Mr Oluwole Ntia, Lekki Gardens’ Group Head of Marketing Operations, who received the award. “We do things well, do things right and protect the resources our customers entrust to us.” Founder Dr Richard Nyong has said the same thing for years, in fewer words: “If the customer does not choose you, you do not get paid.” So, what do Airtel, Fidelity Bank and Lekki Gardens have in common? When the regulator went looking for the advertisers it could hold up as the standard, it found all three. nigeria.title: FG warns public against NTI admissions, cancels 2026 NCE, degree intake
nigeria.description: By Joseph Erunke, Abuja The Federal Ministry of Education has warned prospective students, parents and the general public against seeking admission into unauthorised National Certificate in Education (NCE) and degree programmes at the National Teachers’ Institute (NTI), Kaduna, following regulatory breaches involving admissions, accreditation and university affiliations. Consequently, all admissions into NTI’s NCE and degree programmes for the 2026 academic session have been cancelled, while the Institute has been directed to discontinue all university affiliations and degree-awarding arrangements, as it is not authorised to award NCE and university degrees. The ministry, in a statement by its Director, Press and Public Relations, Boriowo Folasade, emphasised that no further admissions into the affected programmes, whether full-time, part-time or through Distance Learning Studies (DLS), are permitted. Members of the public are therefore strongly advised not to apply, accept admission offers or make payments for such programmes. According to the statement, “The directive follows violations of the Ministerial Operational Guidelines issued on 12 September 2025. The Ministry clarifies that NCE admissions must comply with applicable Joint Admissions and Matriculation Board (JAMB) requirements and accreditation standards of the National Commission for Colleges of Education (NCCE).” “The National Universities Commission (NUC) is also to notify affected universities and ensure compliance with the directive on NTI’s discontinued degree-awarding arrangements,” the statement added. “To protect innocent students already enrolled, the NCCE will conduct comprehensive accreditation of existing NCE II–IV Distance Learning programmes and study centres across the six geopolitical zones. Eligible students may complete their programmes, subject to accreditation outcomes and regulatory requirements, “it further added. The ministry reiterated that NTI’s statutory mandate remains teacher training, retraining, in-service development and continuous professional development. This includes pedagogical capacity-building and the three-to-six-month Special Abridged Programme for serving teachers with non-education degrees to acquire the professional competencies required for registration with the Teachers Registration Council of Nigeria (TRCN), subject to applicable regulations. The ministry stressed that the intervention is intended to protect students, uphold academic standards and prevent further exposure of prospective applicants to unapproved programmes. It urged the public to verify programme accreditation and admission status through relevant regulatory authorities and official government channels before making enrolment or payment decisions. nigeria.title: FIFA U-17 WWC Final: Nigeria vs Japan – date, time and where to watch
nigeria.description: Nigeria’s Flamingos will face Japan in the final of the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco on Saturday, November 7, as they seek to make history by winning their first title. The final, which will be the 52nd and last match of the tournament, will kick off at 7:30 p.m. Nigerian time at the Mohammed VI Football Complex, Pitch 3, in Rabat. The encounter will be the first meeting between Nigeria and Japan at the FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup and the first time the two countries face each other in a global final. Where to watch Nigeria vs Japan Football fans can watch the final live and for free through FIFA+, with streaming available via DAZN. How Nigeria reached the final Nigeria’s campaign in Morocco did not begin as expected, as the Flamingos suffered a 2-1 defeat to Poland in their opening group match. They subsequently recorded a narrow victory over Puerto Rico before producing one of the tournament’s biggest upsets by defeating defending champions DPR Korea 3-1. The Nigerian side built on that result with victories over Mexico and Venezuela before overcoming Brazil in the semi-finals to secure a historic place in the final. Queen Joseph was particularly impressive against Brazil, scoring a goal and providing an assist to help Nigeria reach their maiden U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Nigeria are the first African country to reach the final of the competition. How Japan reached the final Japan, meanwhile, have been impressive throughout the tournament, winning all their group-stage matches without conceding a goal. Although they fell behind against Kenya in the round of 16, Sadayoshi Shirai’s team recovered to secure a 3-1 victory. They subsequently edged Ghana to reach the semi-finals, where they faced DPR Korea. Japan came from behind in the closing stages, benefiting from a late own goal before winning the contest through a penalty shootout to book their place in a fourth U-17 Women’s World Cup final. Players to watch For Japan, Mei Hanashiro will be one of the players Nigeria must watch closely. The forward has scored four goals and provided one assist at the tournament, making her one of the team’s leading attacking threats. Nigeria will look to Queen Joseph, whose pace and attacking quality have made her one of the standout players of the competition. Her goal and assist against Brazil underlined her importance to the Flamingos’ title ambitions. What the coaches and captains said Japan coach Sadayoshi Shirai said his team were determined to complete their campaign by winning the trophy. “We don’t want to stop here. We’ll continue moving forward, prepare as well as we can for the final, and give everything we have to become world champions.” Japan captain Honoka Yotsumoto also expressed confidence ahead of the encounter. “We’ve managed to overcome barriers that had held us back for so long, one step at a time – that has given us a lot of confidence. nigeria.title: Nigeria Presides Over Key UN Election
nigeria.description: Nigeria has presided over key elections at the United Nations General Assembly’s Fifth Committee, with Mauritania and Israel emerging as beneficiaries of two significant appointments during the 81st Session of the General Assembly. The elections, conducted under the chairmanship of Nigeria’s permanent representative to the United Nations, Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, saw C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania recommended as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission, while Israel’s candidate, Shai Mazai, secured a place on the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. In a demonstration of transparency in the electoral process, Ambassador Ibrahim directed that the ballot boxes be opened before voting commenced, allowing delegates to verify the boxes ahead of the collection of ballots. In the contest for the chairmanship of the International Civil Service Commission, C.D. Mohammed of Mauritania secured 102 votes, defeating Mrs. Maria of Zimbabwe, who polled 82 votes. Having obtained the required majority of 93 votes, Mohammed was recommended by the Fifth Committee to the General Assembly for designation as Chair of the International Civil Service Commission for a four-year term beginning January 1, 2027. In another significant outcome, Israel’s Mr. Shai Mazai secured 134 votes to emerge as the recommended candidate from the Group of Western European and Other States to the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee subsequently recommended his appointment to the committee for a three-year term, also beginning January 1, 2027. The elections formed part of the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119, which covers appointments to fill vacancies in subsidiary organs and other appointments. Other bodies considered during the exercise included the Advisory Committee on Administrative and Budgetary Questions, the Committee on Contributions and the Investment Committee, alongside the International Civil Service Commission and the Independent Audit Advisory Committee. The Fifth Committee, chaired by Ambassador Jimoh Ibrahim, also recommended candidates from other regional groups to the International Civil Service Commission through acclamation, following the absence of contested nominations for the respective seats. At the conclusion of the exercise, Ambassador Ibrahim commended delegates for their patience, cooperation and commitment throughout the electoral process. He also congratulated those recommended for appointment and urged them to uphold the integrity of the Fifth Committee while discharging their responsibilities. The Nigerian diplomat equally acknowledged the contributions of the tellers and officials nominated by Member States to supervise the electoral process. Ambassador Ibrahim subsequently declared the Committee’s consideration of Agenda Item 119 concluded and requested the Rapporteur to communicate its decisions to the General Assembly for further action. entertainment.title: From the Sky to the Earth To You: Earth & Sky by Banke Kuku
entertainment.description: With Earth & Sky , her Spring/Summer 2027 collection, Banke Kuku turns to nature’s most essential cycle: the sky gives rain, the rain feeds the earth, and the earth gives back. Reimagining the water cycle as a circle of life, the collection celebrates the abundance that flows from it. Earth & Sky is built around seven prints in three families. The Sky family is led by the hero print, Bougainvillea Sky, with watercolour bougainvillea, bees, butterflies and birds drifting across a turquoise ground, alongside Dove Sky and Daybreak Sky. The Earth family, Yellow Trumpet and Flower Bud, draws on flowering plants such as Costus spectabilis . The Rain family pairs Raindrop, a glossy, near-photographic print set against the softness of the watercolours, with the Kuku Monogram in fresh colourways. Sky prints are finished with hand-embroidered clouds and raindrops on flowing kaftans and kimono robes. Speaking on the inspiration, Creative Director Banke Kuku shares: “I never start with a sketch. I start with a feeling, and for Earth & Sky, that feeling was abundance. This year I became a mother for the first time, and everywhere I looked, nature was reflecting that same fullness back at me. This is my most personal collection.” A CYCLE OF GIVING BACK In nature, nothing is wasted, and everything returns. Earth & Sky carries that principle as its message: what we take from the earth, we must give back. That principle extends into how Banke Kuku approaches production. The brand maintains a no-waste policy, finding uses for offcuts rather than discarding them, while its seasonless approach allows pieces to remain part of the collection beyond a single season. Banke Kuku also uses digital printing, which consumes less heat and water than conventional printing methods, and continues to reduce its use of man-made fabrics in favour of more conscious material choices. Its commitment to the natural world extends beyond its collections, including its work with the Nigerian Conservation Foundation and its Re-Green Movement, which supports afforestation and the restoration of Nigeria’s natural environment. entertainment.title: Adaugo Nwankpa: What a Career Transition Taught Me About Starting Over
entertainment.description: One year and two months ago, I took a career pivot. I moved from being a digital media professional writing stories, articles and shaping narratives to becoming an analyst in the energy sector, working across the oil and gas and renewable subsectors. The journey across these two industries that are worlds apart has taught me lessons on starting over You are never really starting from scratch No matter what you are starting over at or what you are getting into, it is important to realise that you are never truly starting from zero. Where ‘zero’ means the state of having nothing: skills, experience, network, intelligence, and others. While it may indeed appear that you do not have the things you consider as being critical to starting over, you actually have what you have: the knowledge, skills and experiences that have shaped your life and marked your journey up to this present moment, and this is invaluable. Also, having a strong knowledge of yourself is also an incredible resource when starting over, as it helps you to discern and differentiate challenges that are due to your personality, and challenges that are due to the circumstance of starting over. Your ‘Next Best Move’ is hidden within your network When we think of network, it is easy to limit it to close friends, relatives or even acquaintances. This is quite a restrictive and limiting view of the concept of network. Your network also includes ‘strangers’ and your internet community. In my case, I knew of the opportunity in the energy sector through a friend whom I had met on Instagram. It gets more interesting. By the time I was preparing for my first interview, I knew that I had zero knowledge about the current state of the sector. Thanks again to Instagram, I reached out to someone I followed who I knew worked in the sector, and she offered a free virtual coffee chat. I went into the interview more confident in what value I could offer and what mattered for such a role. Transferable skills are invaluable Prior to my career pivot, my only exposure to the energy sector aside from buying fuel and gas was a seminar paper I had written in my final year investigating annual shifts in fuel pump prices. However, I audited my skills and qualifications and noted that I also had highly transferable skills. I had communication, business development and a good knowledge and expertise in using Canva. For you, it could be international exposure, multiple languages or something else you think is insignificant. entertainment.title: Loving Itohan: Come for the Love Story, Stay for Everything Loving Itohan Says About Grief and Family
entertainment.description: Nancy Isime ‘s first film as executive producer, from GREOH Studios, is a beautifully shot story about the love that holds a family together when life falls apart. Some films you watch. Others stay with you. Loving Itohan is the second kind. It opens like the love story you think you already know: a radiant bride, an Edo wedding, coral beads and gold everywhere. You settle in for romance. Then, slowly, the film shows you its heart, and it is so much bigger than a love story. At its centre is Itohan, played by Nancy Isime, a woman whose world is shaken by loss and by truths she never saw coming. What follows is a story about grief, the quiet kind that stays in a home long after the visitors have gone. It is about family, the people who hold us up and sometimes weigh us down. And it is about love that has to keep choosing to stay, even when it hurts. You will see yourself in it. In the person trying to hold everyone together. In the things left unsaid at the dinner table. In the slow, uneven way healing actually happens. A film that looks as good as it feels The cinematography deserves its own round of applause. Every frame feels deliberate, from the rich reds and golds of Edo tradition to the close, quiet moments where a single look says everything. The camera knows when to celebrate and when to simply sit with a character in her pain. This is a film made for the big screen. There is a reason it all feels so assured. Loving Itohan is from GREOH Studios , and Jade studio has never been afraid to go big, with daring, genre-bending stories like Gangs of Lagos. This time, GREOH goes deep instead, trading spectacle for the messy, tender feelings we all carry. True to form, it also hands the director’s chair to a fresh talent, Orobosa Ikponmwen , the latest in a line of new directors the studio has backed, from Kayode Kasum to Loukman Ali. And for Nancy Isime, this is her very first project as an executive producer. You can feel how much of herself she has poured into it, in front of the camera and behind it. Alongside her, Uzor Arukwe, Martha Ehinome Orhiere, Dorathy Bachor, Grace Dein Coker, Chioma Nwosu, Florence Sunday and newcomer Obehi Aburime bring the family to life. Don’t judge it by the trailer If the trailer has you thinking you know where this is going, trust us, you don’t. Go with someone you love. Bring tissues. And maybe call your mum afterwards. Loving Itohan is in cinemas nationwide from 6 November 2026. entertainment.title: Dayo Akinbode: What Travelling to Cuba Taught Me About Money
entertainment.description: I went to Cuba for the salsa, the cigars, the rum and those gorgeous vintage cars. I never imagined that, somewhere between admiring the colourful streets and enjoying the Caribbean sunshine, I would receive an unexpected lesson in money management. Looking back, I can laugh about my experience. But at the time, discovering how much I might have been overpaying left me wondering how much my ignorance had already cost me. Cuba had a way of making me feel as though I had stepped into a film. Imagine standing in a sun-drenched plaza, a Cuban cigar in your hand, the warm Caribbean breeze brushing against your skin, and music floating through the air. Around you, buildings painted in faded yellows, dusty pinks and weathered blues stand proudly, their grand colonial facades and ornate balconies carrying stories from another century. Then comes the rumble of an engine. You turn to see a cherry-red vintage car gliding past, followed by a bubblegum-pink beauty that seems to have driven straight out of the 1950s. Everywhere you look, vibrant colours, rich history and lively movement bring the streets to life And the cars! Oh, the cars! Later, I would find myself riding in a neon-green convertible along the coast, the wind whipping through my hair as the blue Caribbean Sea stretched beside me. I felt wonderfully alive. Cuba was giving me everything I had hoped for: beauty, music, history and the thrill of discovering somewhere different. I was so captivated by everything that I paid little attention to the money in my purse. I visited Cuba in 2019, when the country had two official currencies: the Cuban convertible peso, known as the CUC, and the Cuban peso, known as the CUP. To an unsuspecting tourist like me, this arrangement was a recipe for confusion. I was carrying CUC notes, commonly used by visitors because that is what the banks give you in exchange for your USD notes. The CUC notes looked different from the CUP notes I would later encounter. CUC notes featured monuments, while CUP notes carried the faces of Cuban national heroes, including José Martí and Camilo Cienfuegos. But at the time, I barely noticed the distinction. Money was money, or so I thought. Whenever I needed to pay for something, I reached into my purse, brought out my CUC notes and settled the bill. I was enjoying my holiday and had no reason to suspect my wallet was quietly making it more expensive than necessary. Then, one time, I was given change in a currency different from the familiar CUC. I looked at the notes in my hand and immediately felt that something was wrong. These were not the notes I was accustomed to using. I did not recognise them, and I was not about to walk away with money I did not understand. So, I rejected the change. Imagine my surprise when the cashier and another customer explained to me that the notes were perfectly valid Cuban money! That was when I got my crash course in Cuban economics. sports.title: Ice hockey chiefs mull all 'avenues' for German worlds as Russia waits
sports.description: FILE PHOTO - Czech Republic's Dmitrij Jaskin (L) and Russia's Sergei Plotnikov battle for the puck during the 2019 IIHF Ice Hockey World Championship Bronze medal match ice hockey match between Russia and Czech Republic at the Ondrej Nepela Arena. (is associated with: «Ice hockey chiefs mull all 'avenues' for German worlds as Russia waits») Martti Kainulainen/Lehtikuva/dpa "All available avenues" are being considered by the International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) as it tries to find a way forward after Russia was allowed to compete in the men's world championship in Germany in May. The decision by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) prompted dismay among other nations, sponsors and politicians. Several countries said they would boycott games against Russia at the championship given the ongoing war in Ukraine, while sponsors said they would think about withdrawing. Germany is mulling whether to hand back the hosting rights or not give visas to the Russian team. "While the IIHF continues to disagree with the decision of the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) concerning Russian participation in IIHF Championships, we are taking the necessary steps required by the CAS ruling and reviewing what conditions would need to be met to safeguard our Championships," a statement said on Saturday. "The IIHF must work within the applicable framework while upholding its responsibility to preserve international competition and protect the sport as a whole. The IIHF is therefore exploring all available avenues." The federation also confirmed that Belarus, which has helped Russia in its war on Ukraine, remains banned from international ice hockey competition. The International Olympic Committee lifted a ban on the Russian Olympic Committee in July, but it is being left up to individual sporting bodies if and how Russia is reincorporated, despite the Ukraine war still raging after four years. The IIHF opted to continue to exclude Russian teams on security grounds, but Russia appealed to the world's top sports court and won. The ruling could have implications for other sports.

sports.title: Jacob Warren returning to old form in return from injury for Mason football
sports.description: MASON — Jacob Warren had hopes of contributing as a running back or linebacker this fall for the Mason football team as it chased its goals. But those hopes took an early hit when Warren broke his left ankle during a four-way scrimmage in August. The break wasn't severe enough where Warren held out hope he could potentially return to the field this season. And that opportunity has come in the MHSAA playoffs. Warren has scored touchdowns the last two weeks while helping Mason capture a fifth district title in six years. That included having four carries for 59 yards and a TD in a 49-0 win over Fenton in a Division 3 district final Friday, Nov. 6. "I'm really lucky my injury was the best it could have been for the situation," Warren said. "I'm just so blessed to be able to be back on the field. "I'm so lucky to have the support system I have around me and the family, friends and coaches that supported me all the 10 weeks I was out. It's so awesome to be back on the football field." Warren has 10 carries for 110 yards and the two TDs the last two weeks. Mason coach Gary Houghton sensed Warren was getting back to his old form in recent practices and said his presence gives the Bulldogs another threat in the backfield to complement Troy Peters and Jeffrey Reisner, who each rushed for more than 100 yards Friday. "He's just a very dynamic athlete, a very smart football player and he's patient," Houghton said. "He'll let his blocks develop and he'll accelerate and go. He's just one of the quickest kids I've ever coached and just a really dynamic kid in space." Warren was cleared for a return a few weeks ago and is ready to do whatever is needed to help the Bulldogs try to extend their playoff run a few more weeks. The next step on the journey for Mason is a trip next week to Chelsea, which is where Warren suffered his injury. "I'm stoked," Warren said. "Obviously it sucked in the scrimmage the week before the first game (to get hurt). I'm just so excited to maybe get a little redemption next week. I can't wait." sports.description: Rugby’s Nations Championship bursts back into life as the inaugural edition comes to a conclusion in a busy November. The new competition pits the Six Nations sides against the four Rugby Championship competitors, plus Japan and Fiji, across six matches split evenly across the July and November Test windows. The results of those games will determine each of the 12 teams’ seedings for the finals weekend at Twickenham’s Allianz Stadium , with six matches contested over two days and both team and hemisphere silverware up for grabs. Each entrant will be matched against the equivalent qualifier from the other pool to decide overall placings at the conclusion of a busy year of international action. France and South Africa currently top the two pools, with New Zealand also unbeaten and level on points with the Springboks. Here’s the full competition schedule, and how it will all work: What is the Nations Championship? Announced during the 2023 Rugby World Cup, the new competition will be held every other year and replaces the traditional summer tours and Autumn Nations Series. It is designed to add context to the international calendar, with Fiji and Japan invited to join the Six Nations and Rugby Championship sides to form a top 12. Promotion and relegation is planned for the future with the second-tier Nations Cup, though will not take place in 2026. The entrants are: Northern Hemisphere : France, Ireland, Scotland, Italy, England, Wales. Southern Hemisphere: South Africa, New Zealand, Argentina, Australia, Fiji, Japan. What about the finals weekend? The first finals weekend will be held at Twickenham on the last weekend (27 to 29) of November. Three days of double-headers will be held at the ground, with the first-placed finisher of the Six Nations sides meeting whoever tops the other pool, and so on and so forth down the rankings. The winner of that marquee match will lift the first Nations Championship trophy, while whichever hemisphere – a term used loosely with Japan included in the “southern” section and Fiji hosting their games in the United Kingdom – wins more final matches will also be crowned. The 1st vs 1st match is worth two points, with all other matches in the finals weekend worth one. How can I watch it? Viewers in the United Kingdom will be able to watch every game on ITV after the free-to-air broadcaster struck a deal to show the competition. Langeliers, 28, was born Nov. 18, 1997, in Portland, Oregon, played at Baylor and went ninth overall to the Atlanta Braves in 2019. At sites near the city’s stone ruins, clusters of iron-smelting furnaces survive today as mounds of rubble. At Mashava, a village 25 miles northwest, fragments bear fingermarks of those who long ago smoothed the structures’ clay interiors. Some of the furnaces were nearly an adult’s arm span in width, with walls thick and strong to contain the heat of more than 2,100° Fahrenheit needed to smelt iron. Unlike other furnaces that required workers to force air into them with bellows, these were designed to suck air in, then out through a chimney, no human labor required. technology.description: NHS staff drafted into a helpline after colleagues' health data was exposed online faced distressed callers, safeguarding concerns, and a "serious emotional impact," a review has found. The report [PDF] comes almost exactly a year after the Royal Cornwall Hospitals NHS Trust disclosed a data breach affecting 8,003 people, including current and former trust staff and non-trust workers. A member of the public discovered the exposure in November 2025. An Excel workbook published in response to a Freedom of Information request in February 2023 retained underlying sickness absence records that users could reveal through its pivot tables. Staff assigned to the helpline described difficult calls involving shouting, anger, and distress. Particularly difficult calls involved people distressed by the sensitivity of the disclosures or potentially in danger from domestic abuse. Call handlers said they had to make safeguarding assessments without training or an established process. "Such occurrences of anger or distress were not infrequent, and this reflected the heightened emotions and distress experienced by callers to varying degrees due to the breach," the review noted. "This placed significant emotional burden on individuals working in the contact center, who were not prepared or provided support on how to deal with those." Members of the trust's clinical governance team were told just a day beforehand that they would staff the helpline. Despite their experience dealing with patient trauma, they received little preparation for the calls that followed. "The staff working in the call centers had a short training session and then the calls started coming in within minutes of the team being set up," the review noted. "Some staff had not finished reading the pre-prepared script which had arrived only 30 minutes before the center went live." Most call handlers only learned that their own data had been exposed while already working on the helpline, sometimes minutes before supporting others affected. Call handlers also said they had little choice about taking on the work and were expected to maintain their usual duties alongside it. The review stated that some staff members gave up weekends and worked long past their scheduled hours to meet the demands of both roles. "It's typical NHS, it runs on goodwill," one staffer told the team that compiled the report. The call center was only supposed to run for two weeks in December 2025, but due to the volume of calls, it was eventually stood down after 11 weeks, in February 2026. According to officials speaking at a trust board meeting on Thursday, the review and its findings have since been circulated among staff, and published online. From Finland to Ireland, they suddenly began heating up , many reaching 50C and food worth millions of euros had to be thrown away. But no actual hand was needed to cause the meltdown. This was a cyber-attack, or rather a chain of attacks. Like pretty much everything else in 2026, supermarket freezers are digitally enabled. That makes them smarter and more efficient, but like everything else that is connected to the internet, it also makes them more vulnerable. Russian hacktivists claimed they were behind some of the supermarket sabotage, but no one knows for sure. It could also be Iran, Iranian proxies, North Korea – or unaffiliated bedroom hackers. When Transport for London suffered a devastating hack two years ago, the culprits turned out to be two British teenagers . Governments regularly warn retailers and other companies about cyber-attacks and even provide cyber-defence training to businesses . The lessons of costly ransomware and cyber-attacks also mean many big organisations and retailers have become much better at keeping their payments and logistics systems safe. Despite the ghastly injury, the man was alive and conscious when he arrived. He could still talk and move all four limbs. His doctors described him as being in a state of agitation. On the Glasgow Coma Scale, he scored a 12 (E3 V4 M5) , indicating a "moderate" brain injury, just one point above "mild." He could open his left eye when told, but otherwise kept it closed (E3 score); he could talk and answer questions, but was confused (V4); and he intentionally moved away when pressure was applied to his body (M5). In a report published Friday in BMJ Case Report, his doctors said they were concerned that in his confused, agitated state he may try to pull the knife out on his own. science.title: Star Wars is experiencing a golden age of video games
science.description: After a tumultuous start to EA's rebooted Star Wars Battlefront series, in 2021 Lucasfilm and Disney decided to open up the development of new Star Wars games by bringing in different publishers and studios under the Lucasfilm Games banner. Now, over five years on, we can confidently say we're entering a new golden era of amazing Star Wars games . With LucasArts' successor calling the shots and coordinating a multitude of projects set in a galaxy far, far away, even EA's latest efforts like Squadrons and the Jedi series have taken bigger and bolder swings. Now, in 2026, the full potential of the Star Wars universe has become clearer with specific releases squarely aimed at niche audiences. It's become clear that future Star Wars games needn't be expensive endeavors full of familiar faces or concepts. Star Wars Zero Company and Galactic Racer 's restrained scope and confidence have been infectious, and, as it turns out, they're already recognized by all the parties involved as double-A success stories . Now this is podracing! (Image credit: Secret Mode) A Burnout-inspired Star Wars racer (created by a bunch of ex-Burnout devs) is a fantastic pitch if you know your video games, but looking at EA's recent and current direction, it's easy to see why it didn't happen under their reign. The original Burnout studio, Criterion, would have been an excellent candidate, but instead they were sent to work in the Battlefield mines. Still, someone was interested in the idea, and the end result is glorious. Fast and furious, Star Wars: Galactic Racer ignores recent racing game trends and bets big on arcade-y vibes, uncomplicated controls, and a high skill ceiling that challenges you with extremely high speeds, tight turns, and unexpected interruptions as other drivers try to ruin your day. The not-so-secret sauce, however, was its runs-based structure, which injects the flexibility and replay value of roguelite games into the more traditional arcade racing structure that older gamers are familiar with. (Image credit: EA) Fully confident in its central gameplay idea and devoid of modern live-service baggage, Fuse Games' debut title makes the most of the Star Wars setting within the restrictions of simply making a fun and engaging Star Wars racer. It's almost the same approach we felt in Zero Company, a turn-based tactical strategy-RPG that comes from the minds of another team of ex-triple-A developers. "Star Wars but XCOM" should've happened earlier, but we're glad it did this year, and, unsurprisingly, it's a banger. The correct read of their success should be obvious (and so far, it appears the powers that be are seeing it): Let seasoned and fresh developers cook games they're excited about. science.title: SpaceX launches mystery mission for US Space Force in gorgeous sunset liftoff from California (video, photos)
science.description: null SpaceX just launched a classified mission for the U.S. military. A Falcon 9 rocket lifted off from California's Vandenberg Space Force Base this evening (Nov. 6) at 7:48 p.m. EST (4:48 p.m. local California time; 0048 GMT on Nov. 7), rising into the sky as the sun sank toward the Pacific. The launch kicked off the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force , which we know little about. Neither SpaceX nor the Space Force told us much about USSF-432 beforehand, and we learned tonight; SpaceX cut its webcast off about 10 minutes into the flight, shortly after the Falcon 9's first stage came back to Earth for a landing. A SpaceX Falcon 9 rocket launches the USSF-432 mission for the U.S. Space Force from Vandenberg Space Force Base on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) That touchdown occurred aboard the SpaceX droneship "Of Course I Still Love You," which was stationed downrange in the Pacific Ocean. It wrapped up the eighth flight for this particular booster, which is designated 1095. The Falcon 9's upper stage, meanwhile, continued carrying its mystery payload skyward. It could be headed to low Earth orbit , outside observers speculate. "It is possibly a batch of classified LEO satellites for the USSF's Space Based Sensing and Targeting (SBST) portfolio based on SpaceX's Starshield satellite bus, based on locations of rocket stage drop zones being exact fits with previous Starlink Group 15 launches," NextSpaceflight.com wrote in a mission description . Starlink is SpaceX's LEO broadband megaconstellation, which consists of more than 11,000 active satellites. Starshield is a similar system designed to provide services to the U.S. military and its allies. Starshield satellites are believed to be based heavily on the Starlink spacecraft bus. The Falcon 9's first stage after its landing on Nov. 6, 2026. (Image credit: SpaceX) Previous Booster 1095 missions GPS-III 8 | 6 Starlink missions USSF-432 was the 119th Falcon 9 launch of 2026, and the 14th national-security flight of the rocket so far this year. The vast majority of Falcon 9 missions in 2026 — more than 70% — have been devoted to building out the Starlink megaconstellation. SpaceX has also launched six other missions this year. science.title: On this day in space! Nov. 6, 1572: A German astronomer discovers the Tycho supernova with the naked eye, but everyone thought the cosmic explosion was a 'new star'
science.description: null On Nov. 6, 1572, the German astronomer Wolfgang Schulër observed a supernova with his bare eyes. He spotted the exploding star in the constellation Cassiopeia. It was as bright as Venus and could even be seen during the day. Astronomers were really confused, because it looked like a star just appeared out of nowhere. Schulër may have been the first to see it, but the Danish astronomer Tycho Brahe is widely credited for the discovery. Brahe studied it in detail and wrote a whole book about this so-called "new star." It then became known as "Tycho's Star." At the time, supernovas had not yet been discovered. Tycho's Star was finally classified as a supernova in the 1940s. Scientists now think it was a small star called a white dwarf that exploded thousands of years ago. Because Tycho's Star is 13,000 light-years from Earth, it took a while before anyone could see it. The Tycho supernova remnant as seen by the Chandra X-ray space telescope. (Image credit: X-ray: NASA/CXC/RIKEN & GSFC/T. Sato et al; Optical: DSS) Why it mattered The Tycho supernova, known technically as SN 1572 , is known today as a Type Ia supernova, which is a star explosion in a binary star system in which a white dwarf star draws material away from its partner, then explodes. But in 1572, the Tycho supernova appeared as something very different: a bright new star. While Schulër was first, other astronomers also observed the apparently new star in the sky. Tycho Brahe's numerous observations are the most well known, in no small part becuause he wrote a book all about them in "De Stella Nova" (Latin for "On The New Star." At the time, the prevailing theory among scientists was that the stars were unchanging, yet here was a new star -- a changed sky. "The 16th century exploding star, which appeared in the constellation Cassiopeia , was seen in daylight for about two weeks, and remained visible to the naked eye for 16 months," the University of California Berkeley wrote in 2004 . "Brahe's meticulous record of the brightening and dimming of the supernova now allows astronomers to identify its 'light signature" as that of a Type Ia supernova." "This was at the end of the Dark Ages in Europe, and these observations were an important piece of evidence that the heavens were not immutable," astronomer Alex Filippenko, who led a 2004 study on the origins of the Tycho supernova, said at the time . Today, astronomers are closely watching another star that might explode. Called T Corona Borealis , or the Blaze Star , the object is expected to be on the verge of exploding in a nova (a star explosion that is smaller than a supernova and may not destroy the star). is one of 11 known stars observed to have recurring nova explosions within gaps of 100 years or so. science.title: What's that bright 'star' in the early morning sky? It's not a star at all!
science.description: null Early morning risers heading to work or school before sunrise are likely to notice a very bright, star-like object appearing low in the east-southeast sky just before sunrise. What is somewhat amazing is that just a couple of weeks ago this object wasn't there at all, but now it literally stands out with such brilliance as to almost command the attention of commuters who might be traveling in an easterly direction to "Look at me!" The object in question is, of course, the planet Venus, which is currently amid one of its most spectacular forays into the morning sky, literally "vaulting up" into prominence. On Oct. 24, Venus came to inferior conjunction, passing between the Earth and sun and shifting from the evening into the morning sky. And the view is only going to get better in the days and weeks to come! Ascending in the morning In terms of morning visibility, Venus is now in a literal and figurative sense "rising to the occasion." It's now rising before the break of dawn, more than 90 minutes before sunrise. From here on, it will rise three minutes earlier each day, so that by Dec. 17 it will rise 3 hours and 50 minutes before sunrise and blaze in a completely dark sky for more than two hours before the first vestige of morning twilight. It will reach peak brilliance on Nov. 29, when it will shine at an eye-popping magnitude of -4.9. That's 12 times brighter than its nearest planetary competitor, Jupiter and a full 25 times more dazzling than Sirius, the brightest of all stars. If you live in a rural location with no light pollution to interfere, you might be able to make out that it is casting a visible shadow and if you follow it right on through sunrise, it will be evident to your naked eye in full daylight: a tiny white speck plainly evident against the blue daytime sky. In a way, we could even regard Venus as this year's version of a "Christmas Star," glowing with stunning radiance ". . . in the east" like the biblical quote mentioned in St. Matthew. What goes up, must come down After reaching its high point in terms of morning visibility in mid-December, Venus will start a long, slow slide back toward the sun, rising about 1½ minutes later each morning from New Year's Day through late March. By then, Venus will be coming up as dawn is breaking, roughly 100 minutes before sunrise. Venus will continue to get gradually lower and rise progressively later during the spring and by late June it will be coming up less than an hour before sunrise, ultimately vanishing into the bright dawn twilight by July. Venus will then go on a "summer sabbatical" of sorts and will not reappear again until about this time next year when it will begin a very fine evening apparition. So, if any of your friends or relatives remark to you that they saw a "strange UFO" on the way to work or school recently, you now can set them straight. It's not E.T. It's only Venus.
